title: Problem Statement
content: Erdős Problem #412 asks whether all iterated sum-of-divisors sequences eventually merge. Given any two starting points m,n ≥ 2, does there exist i,j such that σᵢ(m) = σⱼ(n)? Communicated to Erdős by van Wijngaarden in the 1950s. Selfridge's numerical evidence suggests NO, but the problem remains OPEN.

title: Sum of Divisors Function
content: We define σ(n) as the sum of all divisors of n, using Nat.divisors to get the finite set of divisors and summing with Finset.sum. For example: σ(6) = 1 + 2 + 3 + 6 = 12. Verified computationally for σ(1)=1, σ(2)=3, σ(6)=12, σ(12)=28, σ(28)=56.

title: Iterated Sigma
content: The k-th iterate of σ: σ₀(n) = n and σₖ(n) = σ(σₖ₋₁(n)). Uses Function.iterate from Mathlib. Example sequences verified: from 2: 2→3→4→7→8→15; from 3: 3→4→7→8→15. The sequences from 2 and 3 merge at step 1!

title: σ-Equivalence and the Conjecture
content: Two numbers m, n are σ-equivalent if their iterated sequences eventually meet: ∃ i j, σᵢ(m) = σⱼ(n). The Erdős412Conjecture states all integers m, n ≥ 2 are σ-equivalent — that there is essentially one universal sequence all iterated σ-sequences eventually join.

title: Verified Equivalences
content: Four σ-equivalences proved computationally via native_decide: 2≡3 (σ₁(2)=3), 2≡4 (σ₂(2)=4), 5≡6 (σ(5)=6), 7≡8 (σ(7)=8). For primes p, σ(p) = p+1, giving immediate merges with p+1.

title: Aliquot Sum Connection
content: The aliquot sum s(n) = σ(n) - n is the sum of proper divisors. Perfect numbers satisfy s(n) = n (verified: s(6)=6, s(28)=28). Problem #412 uses σ (including n), not s (excluding n), but the concepts are related.

title: Growth Properties
content: Two key growth results proved: (1) sigma_ge_succ: σ(n) ≥ n+1 for n ≥ 2, proved by showing {1,n} ⊆ divisors(n) and bounding the sum. (2) sigma_gt: σ(n) > n for n ≥ 2, an immediate corollary. These show iterated sequences are strictly increasing.

title: No Periodicity
content: IsSigmaPeriodic defines σ-periodic numbers (σₖ(n) = n for some k ≥ 1). Theorem no_sigma_periodic_step1 proves σ₁(n) > n for n ≥ 2, ruling out fixed points and showing sequences grow without bound.

title: Summary Theorem
content: erdos_412_summary combines three proved results: (1) σ(n) > n for all n ≥ 2, (2) 2 and 3 are σ-equivalent, (3) σ₁(n) > n for all n ≥ 2. Proved via ⟨sigma_gt, equiv_2_3, no_sigma_periodic_step1⟩.
